issues.description:
Element: Farm.addAnimal(Animal)
Problem statement UML: The UML diagram in problem_statement.md marks addAnimal(animal: Animal):void with a '-' (private) visibility marker.
Problem statement text & examples: The textual instructions and the example Main usage demonstrate that addAnimal should be callable from outside the Farm (i.e., public). The tasks description (Part 3) explicitly documents addAnimal(Animal a) adds an animal to the list.
Template repository: The template Farm.java does not provide an addAnimal method (left for students to implement), but the scaffolding and Main example imply it must be public.
Solution repository: The solution implements addAnimal as public (public void addAnimal(Animal animal)).
How this blocks/confuses students: The UML's '-' private visibility conflicts with the textual description, example Main, and the solution. Students reading the UML might implement addAnimal as private (or be unsure whether it should be public), which would prevent calls from Main and contradict the intended API, causing confusion and possible failing tests or compilation issues when following the example usage.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the visibility consistent: update the UML in problem_statement.md to mark addAnimal(Animal) as public ('+') so it matches the textual instructions, the Main example, and the solution. Additionally, update the template Farm.java scaffold to include a public addAnimal(Animal animal) method signature (with a TODO body) to make the expected public API explicit to students.
